description: Building an interactive tactical surface navigation and survival guide for astronauts conducting Marswalks in Jezero Crater. Our team combines geospatial mapping, telemetry monitoring, and modern web tech to make planetary exploration safer.
summary:
The Mars EVA Navigation System is an interactive tactical surface navigation console and environmental telemetry HUD designed for astronauts conducting extravehicular activity (EVA) in Jezero Crater, Mars. 

Addressing the "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map" challenge, the platform merges orbital satellite basemaps from NASA Mars Trek with ground-level science waypoints from the Perseverance rover. Crew members can point-and-click to map traverse routes while the system automatically calculates real-time oxygen burn rates, walking time under Martian gravity, battery drain, and terrain slope hazards. Integrated live space weather feeds from NASA's DONKI API actively monitor solar flares and coronal mass ejections to protect astronauts from hazardous surface radiation.
details:
What It Does and How It Works:

The Mars EVA Navigation System provides an astronaut tactical visor and habitat mission planning console centered on Jezero Crater (the landing site of NASA's Perseverance rover).

Astronauts and flight controllers can select waypoints across the crater floor—from the landing site at Octavia E. Butler Landing to the Western Delta front and Séítah dunes. As routes are plotted, a client-side geodesic algorithm (scaled to Mars's 3,389.5 km mean radius) computes the total distance, walking time adjusted for 0.38g Martian locomotion, oxygen consumption against an 8-hour PLSS backpack capacity, and battery depletion.

An interactive SVG elevation profile renders the terrain cross-section (-2680m in Séítah to -2520m on the delta rim) and highlights hazardous slopes exceeding safe 12° thresholds. Simultaneously, the app interfaces with NASA's DONKI API to monitor active coronal mass ejections and solar flares, scaling surface radiation telemetry and triggering shelter advisories when thresholds are exceeded.

Tools and Languages:

- Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite

- Mapping: Leaflet.js with custom NASA WMTS tile layer integration and native-zoom upscaling

- Spatial Math: Turf.js with planetary radius transformation

- Styling: Tailwind CSS, JetBrains Mono and Space Grotesk typography

- Cloud Deployment: Vercel Global Edge Network

Intended Impact:

Future crewed missions to Mars will face extreme operational isolation with communication delays up to 20 minutes to Earth. This tool gives astronauts autonomous, localized decision-making power to navigate safely, protect their life-support margins, and maximize science return without waiting for mission control in Houston.

Creativity and Considered Factors:

Unlike standard static map viewers, our system treats navigation as an integrated survival equation: terrain slope, oxygen consumption, battery limits, and cosmic radiation are unified into a single dark-mode HUD designed specifically for low-light habitat and spacesuit visor displays.
